chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “Inquiry is only to us regarding the halal (permissible) and the haram (forbidden); but as for prophethood, then no.”

key_terms.النُّبُوَّةُ: prophethood, the office of a prophet
key_terms.الْحَرَامِ: that which is forbidden in the Sacred Law
key_terms.الْحَلَالِ: that which is permissible in the Sacred Law
key_terms.الْوُقُوفُ: referring matters for clarification and authoritative determination
key_terms.عَلَيْنَا: to us, meaning the Ahl al-Bayt as the locus of religious reference

ai.seo_question: Do the Imams (عليهم السلام) claim prophethood, or is their authority limited to halal and haram?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between the religious authority of the Imams (عليهم السلام) in clarifying halal and haram and the exclusive station of prophethood. It affirms their authoritative role in guidance and law while denying that they possess nubuwwah.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, the inquiring is to us<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Permissible and the Prohibition, but, as for the Prophet-hood (being for us<sup>asws</sup>), so no (it is not)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayrfrom al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“To refer to us (as the Divine authorities) is valid only in finding the lawful and unlawful matters. To refer to us as prophet-hood is not valid.”
